name: Ritual spoon or ladle
definition: Spoon or ladle made to pour or offer water, ghee or a sacrament in a rite (achamani, fire-offering ladle, communion spoon named forms).
reason: Handled implement no hand-implement kind covers; sold by shops as its own item across traditions.

name: Miniature stupa
definition: Small model of a stupa or chorten made to stand on an altar as a sacred focus, filled with relics or mantras or not (chorten a named form).
reason: A three-dimensional sacred focus that is not a figure, cross or set; a reliquary only when made to show a relic.

name: Host vessel
definition: Lidded cup, bowl or box made to hold consecrated or unconsecrated hosts (ciborium, pyx, host box named forms).
reason: Church-supply shops list ciboria and host containers apart from chalices; ritual cup holds drink, monstrance shows the host.

name: Alms box
definition: Box, plate or basket made to collect money given as alms, charity or offering in religious practice (church collection box, tzedakah box, saisen box named forms).
reason: Set out to receive offerings, like F4.4.3 vessels, but a slotted or lidded money container; sold in church and Judaica shops.

candidate: Havdalah spice box (split from Havdalah set)
name: Spice box [besamim box]
definition: Small box or tower made to hold fragrant spices smelled in the Havdalah rite (besamim box a named form).
reason: Judaica shops sell spice boxes as their own department (memo S13); no vessel kind covers it. No logged page: attest in HV_NK.

name: Ritual washing cup
definition: Cup, usually two-handled, made to pour water over the hands in ritual washing (netilat yadayim cup a named form).
reason: Ritual cup is for drink; Judaica shops list washing cups apart and buyers compare them by material and design.
